title: Introvert or Extrovert. Which One Are You?

image.attribution: Elvert Barnes from Hyattsville MD, USA / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.0

main_content:
You are invited to a large party. Loud music is playing, and lots of people are dancing.

What do you do? Do you mingle all night and talk to as many people as you can?

Or do you prefer to have one-on-one conversations with just a few people? Or perhaps you cannot wait to go home early and relax by yourself.

Which of these people sounds most like you?

If you said Person A (the first), you are probably more extroverted. If you said Person B (the second), you are probably more introverted.

Introverts may be viewed as quiet, shy and timid.

Extroverts may be viewed as bold, confident, loud and full of energy.

Introverted and extroverted people may fit those descriptions. But these same descriptions do not define introversion and extroversion properly.

People who consider themselves introverts may say they “need to be alone” or that being in large crowds makes them tired. However, introverts may still love being social.

Extroverts may say, “I don’t need ‘alone time.’ I feel more relaxed being around other people.” Even so, extroverts can still feel unsure among other people.
